evals.name: sanity-slack-audit
evals.prompt: our company blog is on sanity (next.js frontend, about 80 posts) and honestly nobody has touched most of them in a year. i have search console api access and we live in slack. i want a weekly job that tells us which old posts are worth updating and suggests the actual fix, but i do NOT want an llm editing our site on its own. can you build that
evals.expected_output: A weekly audit that pulls 28-day and previous-28-day search data, scores each post by opportunity (recover / ctr / rank) rather than age, drafts one-swap edits, posts Approve/Edit/Skip cards to Slack, and applies approved edits through a separate handler that holds the Sanity write token and re-validates before writing.
assertions: Ranks posts by estimated click headroom, not by age or last-modified date
Scores each post on three distinct levers (lost clicks, page-one click-through gap, page-two rank gap) and uses the largest to choose the kind of fix
Uses an expected click-through-by-position curve to estimate the click-through gap
Drops or separately labels posts with too few impressions instead of ranking them by click-through rate
A measured traffic loss requires both an absolute and a proportional drop
The agent or LLM step has no CMS write access; a separate handler performs the write after a human approves
The approve handler re-validates the stored suggestion (for example that the original text is still present) before writing
Suggested edits are limited to SEO title, SEO description, or a single exact phrase or link swap
Approval is locked so two clicks cannot both publish
Refuses to publish when the post has an unsaved draft in Sanity
Fixes the before-snapshot's date window at the moment an approved edit goes live (numbers fetched then, or later for those stored dates), not from the time a later job runs
Records blog-wide numbers for the same dates as a control

evals.name: mdx-git-solo
evals.prompt: solo dev here. my blog is just mdx files in my next.js repo, deployed on vercel, maybe 25 posts. no slack, no cms. i exported my search console data as csv (queries.csv and pages.csv in ./data). i rank for a bunch of stuff around position 8-15 but get basically no clicks. what should i fix and what should i write next? set up something i can rerun every week
evals.expected_output: A rerunnable script working from the CSV exports that scores posts by opportunity and lists near-miss queries with no dedicated post, with thresholds scaled to a small blog; suggestions arrive as pull requests (one per suggestion) so merging is the approval, and a table or file records before-snapshots for later readings. No Slack or CMS is introduced.
assertions: Works from the CSV exports without requiring Search Console API access
Does not require Slack or a CMS; uses pull requests or an equivalent git-native review step as the approval surface
Scores posts by click headroom using position and impressions, not by age
Scales the impression and drop thresholds down for a small blog, or tells the user to
Identifies near-miss queries (meaningful impressions, roughly positions 5-20, no dedicated post) as the source of new post topics
Checks new topics against existing posts so a new post does not compete with one the site already ranks with
Presents the opportunity number as an ordering estimate, not a traffic forecast
Sets up a way to compare a changed post against the rest of the blog over the same dates
Keeps each suggestion small enough to review (one change per pull request or equivalent)

evals.name: generator-gates-and-measurement
evals.prompt: we already have a script that drafts blog posts from keyword ideas with claude and pushes them to contentful as drafts. two problems: (1) last month it published a post with a code sample that doesn't exist in our sdk, and another that's basically a duplicate of a post we already rank #4 for. (2) my boss wants to know if any of the 30 seo edits we made in q3 actually worked and i have no idea how to answer. how do i fix the pipeline and how should we be measuring this
evals.expected_output: Automated gates in front of the CMS write (code provenance requiring a docs URL per snippet, cannibalization against existing ranking posts, plus strategy and structure), a bounded redraft limit, cannibalization treated as non-retryable and handed to the audit; and a measurement design with before-snapshots, a blog-wide control over the same dates, 28 and 56 day readings and a cooldown, with an honest note that past edits without snapshots can only be reconstructed approximately.
assertions: Adds a code check that runs before the draft is saved: every snippet must carry the docs URL it was copied from, or be compiled or type-checked against the real SDK, or both
Adds a cannibalization gate that checks target queries against posts the site already ranks with
On a cannibalization failure the pipeline does not rephrase and retry; it identifies the existing post and routes it to an edit instead
Limits redraft attempts to a small fixed number, then stops without saving a draft
Gates run before anything is written to Contentful
Keeps subjective writing quality out of the hard gates (a checklist or review step instead)
Measurement compares each edited post with blog-wide numbers over the same dates, not only with its own before/after
Uses two follow-up readings (around 28 and 56 days) rather than one
Adds a cooldown that blocks (not merely warns about) a second edit to a post inside its measurement window
Says that the Q3 edits can only be assessed approximately, because no before-snapshot or control was recorded at the time
Warns against reading percentage changes on small click counts
